Blindly benchmark age-splitting methods against a single-age schedule

Source: R/age.R
benchmark_age_split.Rd

Aggregate an independent single-age population schedule to source_breaks, restore it with each method, and compare the restored schedule with the held-out source. This provides a reproducible validation workflow for an official single-age population series without allowing the target series to be used as a "reference" schedule.

Usage

benchmark_age_split(
  population,
  source_breaks = c(0, 1, seq(5, 85, 5)),
  methods = c("linear", "sprague"),
  reference = NULL,
  cases = NULL,
  stdpop = NULL,
  mp = 1e+05,
  high_age = "keep",
  pclm_control = list()
)

Arguments

population

Held-out single-age population schedule. Supply a named numeric vector or a data frame accepted by expand_age_pop(). Ages at or above the final source_breaks value are treated as the open group.

source_breaks

Lower bounds used to blind the held-out schedule.

methods

Character vector of methods passed to expand_age_pop().

reference

Independent reference schedule used only by the "reference" method.

cases

Optional held-out single-age case schedule. If supplied, age-standardized-rate bias is calculated using the restored population.

stdpop

Optional single-age standard-population weights for ASR. Equal weights are used when cases is supplied without stdpop.

mp

Multiplier for the ASR, defaulting to 100,000.

high_age

High-age configuration passed to expand_age_pop().

pclm_control

PCLM control settings passed to expand_age_pop().

Value

A data frame with MAE, RMSE, total variation distance, ASR bias, maximum source-group error, number of negative values, and available uncertainty-interval diagnostics. The restored schedules are stored in the estimates attribute; the error for every effective source group is stored in the group_errors attribute.
